# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** MedStar Family Choice DC — Member Appeals
Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or the address given when I call the number on the back of my insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

**From:** Avery Lawson
Member ID: W601208268
[Your mailing address]
[Your phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-06 — Reference number POC-0948C5760B-46622**
**Service denied:** Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
**Governing policy:** *Utilization Management Criteria* — https://www.medstarfamilychoicedc.com/-/media/project/mho/mfcdc/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115dc_utilization-management-criteria.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which MedStar Family Choice DC denied on 2026-08-06 under reference number POC-0948C5760B-46622. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the imaging and clinical records in my file describe a specific, surgically treatable injury, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

This appeal is timely. My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-02**.

## The plan's own policy, and what it does and does not say

The plan's *Utilization Management Criteria* policy states:

> "MedStar Family Choice DC follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making across all service types."

and

> "MedStar Family Choice DC prior-authorization decisions for medical and behavioral health services, including residential treatment are based on the following criteria:"

I want to be straightforward with you about the limits of what I can quote. That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of criteria that I have not been given, and the policy elsewhere refers to further criteria and processes that are likewise not reproduced in the material available to me. The policy text I have does not state any imaging standard, threshold, finding, or grade that my MRI was measured against. So I cannot show you a quoted imaging rule and match my records to it line by line — because the plan has not quoted one to me. The denial notice refers generally to the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria without identifying the specific criterion my imaging is said to have failed.

The policy does, however, tell me that those criteria exist and are obtainable:

> "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request."

and

> "To request specific utilization management criteria or to speak with a Medical Director, please contact us by phone during our normal business hours, 8:00 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday through Friday at 1-(855)-798-4244."

## Request for the criteria applied to my determination

**I am requesting, in writing, the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on to deny this request.** Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules require the plan to provide me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on in making the adverse determination. I am therefore asking MedStar Family Choice DC to send me the full text of the criteria applied to my determination — and, if those criteria come from a licensed clinical criteria product such as InterQual, the specific subset and edition used — together with the list of criteria introduced by the policy language quoted above. The plan holds these documents; I do not. Without them I cannot know which imaging finding the reviewer expected to see and did not, and neither the plan nor I can confirm that my records were measured against the correct standard.

## What my records show

These are the facts as they appear in the prior authorization packet:

- **Imaging (MRI of the knee, 2026-05-28):** displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking; articular cartilage preserved, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1.
- **Symptoms:** 24 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 16 weeks, 2026-03-10 to 2026-06-30, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication and injection:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief; corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-26 giving 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Function:** locking and giving way; unable to squat or kneel; limited to level walking.
- **Exam:** positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
- **Other:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery.

The MRI does not describe an ambiguous or incidental finding. It describes a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and the mechanical symptoms it predicts — locking and giving way — are the symptoms documented on my exam and in my history. The imaging and the clinical picture agree with each other.

The policy also states:

> "Upon review for medical necessity, requests for ongoing services or treatment that have not demonstrated improvement in condition or benefit to the Enrollee will be subject to denial as not medically necessary."

My record is the picture of non-surgical treatment that has not produced improvement or benefit: 20 physical therapy visits over 16 weeks, 6 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection that gave 2 weeks of partial relief. Continuing those same measures is what my record shows has not worked. The surgery is the change in course.

I would also note that the MRI reports articular cartilage preserved and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 — that is, the imaging identifies the meniscal tear as the problem to be addressed.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask MedStar Family Choice DC to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-06 (reference POC-0948C5760B-46622) and authorize CPT 29881;
2. Provide me in writing, free of charge, the full text of the criteria applied to my determination — including the subset and edition, if a licensed criteria product such as InterQual was used — along with the specific criterion my imaging was found not to meet;
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer, and identify that reviewer's specialty in the response; and
4. If the denial is upheld, state plainly which imaging finding the criteria require, which finding in my 2026-05-28 MRI was found insufficient, and my further appeal rights, including external review.

I have included the records referenced above. Please contact me at [your phone number] or [your email address] if anything further is needed.

Thank you for taking a second look at this.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
**Avery Lawson**
Member ID: W601208268
Reference number: POC-0948C5760B-46622
[Your mailing address]
[Your phone number]
[Your email address]

**Enclosures:** MRI report dated 2026-05-28; physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-10 to 2026-06-30, 20 visits); office notes from Okafor, MD; record of corticosteroid injection 2026-05-26; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-06

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that your plan will approve coverage.*
